item.title: Hindu pilgrims on an arduous trek are among Nepal's missing
item.description: Among the hundreds still missing on Nepal's border with China are Hindus from India and beyond, participating in a journey of devotion to a sacred mountain.

item.title: How one church in Nashville celebrated Dolly Parton's life on Sunday
item.description: Since Dolly Partons' death, many in Nashville, where she lived for years, have praised her as an example of how to live a Christian life. One church even held a communion service in Dolly's honor.
item.content:encoded: Since Dolly Partons' death, many in Nashville, where she lived for years, have praised her as an example of how to live a Christian life. One church even held a communion service in Dolly's honor.

item.title: Greetings from Karbala, Iraq, where millions gathered for a Shia pilgrimage
item.description: Pilgrims came to Iraq from all over the world in August. Many Iraqi and Iranian pilgrims walked hundreds of miles in extreme heat to mark the event. Outside the shrines, the atmosphere is almost festive.

item.title: Holy wit: How comedians turn personal faith into perfect comedy
item.description: Since the book of Genesis, religion has been an irresistible subject for reliable laughs. But the jokes often land best when comics reflect on their own faith traditions.

item.title: A Paris cafe-bar is a longtime gathering spot for older men of different faiths
item.description: A cafe in one of Paris' most historically diverse neighborhoods has long been a gathering spot for Muslims and Jews of Tunisian origin, who've been getting together for decades to play cards and chat.

item.title: Living with nuns: Priced out of D.C., young women found low rent with unlikely roommates
item.description: For 10 years, a Catholic-run home offered young women an affordable place to live in the nation's capital as they studied and launched careers. Now, that community is saying goodbye.

item.title: Meditation, hunt-a-monk and two hours of silence: Welcome to Buddhist summer camp
item.description: At Dharma Camp is in the foothills of Oregon's Cascade Mountains, campers make friendship bracelets, play games and try to keep their fidgety bodies still enough to meditate. For some teens, summers camps can be an important time to explore their religious beliefs outside of home.

item.title: A former nun explains why she ran away from her 'Cloistered' life
item.description: Catherine Coldstream entered a Carmelite monastery at age 24, and lived a life of prayer and obedience for 12 years. Her memoir is Cloistered: My Years as a Nun. Originally published March 20, 2024.

item.description: Sisters Theresa Alethia and Danielle Lussier call themselves the Sisters of the Little Way of Beauty, Truth and Goodness. Their order plans to help victims of abuse.

item.title: These Catholic sisters want to start an order for clergy abuse survivors
item.description: There are nearly 2,000 communities of religious sisters and nuns in the Catholic church. Two nuns in Kentucky want to start the first devoted to ministering to people harmed by abuse in the church.
